verifiedProperties.noUnboundedLoopsNote: batchMint loops `count` times over caller-supplied `count` (BatchMint__ZeroCount only checks > 0; no upper bound). Each iteration is an external mint call that pulls funds, so it is self-limiting by cost rather than a free DoS — see LOCAL-001.
verifiedProperties.checkedArithmeticNote: Solidity ^0.8.20, no unchecked blocks, no assembly.
verifiedProperties.reentrancyGuardedNote: batchMint has NO nonReentrant guard. It makes external calls (safeTransferFrom, forceApprove, nftMinter.mint x count, nudge safeTransfer to recipient, dust safeTransfer to msg.sender). Reentrancy exploitability deferred to interaction analysis (depends on minter/dispatcher/token callback behaviour).
verifiedProperties.accessControlNote: batchMint is intentionally permissionless (whenNotPaused only). All setters are onlyOwner; pause/unpause are onlyPauser.

localFindings.description: for-loop runs `count` times with no upper bound; `count` is caller-controlled (only checked != 0). Each iteration pulls the dispatcher price from msg.sender, so an attacker pays for every iteration; this self-limits a gas-griefing DoS but a careless large `count` can OOG and revert the whole batch atomically (no partial state). Not exploitable as a fund-loss/DoS-on-others vector locally.
localFindings.recommendation: Optional: cap `count` to a sane MAX_BATCH to give callers a clean revert instead of OOG. Not security-critical.

localFindings.description: batchMint performs multiple external token/minter calls (including a transfer to caller-chosen `recipient` for the nudge and a dust refund to msg.sender) without a nonReentrant modifier. CEI is mostly respected (allowance revoked before nudge; dust sweep last) and balances are re-read fresh each call, but the nudge transfer to an arbitrary `recipient` followed by the dust sweep is a callback surface. Exploitability requires knowing recipient/token callback semantics -> DEFERRED to interaction analysis. Sibling NFTStaker uses nonReentrant on every user entry point; BatchNFTMinter diverges.
localFindings.recommendation: Consider adding OZ ReentrancyGuard.nonReentrant to batchMint for parity with NFTStaker, or document why it is safe given full-balance-read nudge semantics.

localFindings.description: paymentToken is derived from INFTMinterV2(tokenMinter).configs(dispatcherIndex) -> dispatcher.primeToken(). Both the minter and dispatcherIndex are owner-pinned, so this is a trusted derivation, NOT a caller-controlled one (this is the H-01 fix). The configs() tuple destructure ignores price/growthBasisPoints/disabled; BatchNFTMinter never checks `disabled` or `price > 0` itself and relies entirely on the inner mint() to revert. Whether price==0 is reachable is an interaction-level concern (see H-01 read in summary).
localFindings.recommendation: No local action required; flagged as trust assumption for interaction analysis.

externalEntryPoints.function: batchMint(uint256 count, address recipient, uint256 paymentAmount)
externalEntryPoints.stateChangesNote: No contract storage is mutated by batchMint; all effects are external token transfers and allowance toggles. State that gates behaviour (tokenMinter, dispatcherIndex, nudgeSize, nudgePaymentToken) is read-only here.
externalEntryPoints.valueTokenFlows: Pulls paymentAmount of derived paymentToken from msg.sender. Pays inner dispatcher price x count (via minter, funds flow msg.sender->minter pull-through). Pays out FULL nudgePaymentToken balance to recipient when gate clears. Refunds surplus paymentToken (>= DUST_THRESHOLD=1e6 wei) to msg.sender. No native ETH (non-payable).

externalEntryPoints.note: NEW in 031ffda. 0 = disabled sentinel. No validation that index is registered or that resolved price>0.

externalEntryPoints.function: rescueERC20(IERC20 token, address to, uint256 amount)
externalEntryPoints.note: Stays callable while paused. Owner can withdraw the nudge pot directly (acknowledged centralization).

externalCalls.notes: Owner-pinned via setTokenMinter. address(0) disables batchMint. Concrete impl is sibling yield-claim-nft NFTMinterV2.
Resolved from tokenMinter.configs(dispatcherIndex), NOT caller-supplied. As trusted as the owner-pinned minter's config table. primeToken() determines which ERC20 is pulled from msg.sender.
Derived, not caller-chosen. Assumed standard ERC20. forceApprove(max) then forceApprove(0) brackets the loop. FOT handling lives in NFTMinterV2 (balance-before/after), not here.
Owner-pinned. Full balance paid to caller-chosen recipient when gate clears. Must differ from paymentToken (else up-front revert).
Fully caller-controlled. Receives minted NFTs AND the entire nudge pot. Callback surface for the nudge transfer (see LOCAL-002).

nudgeMechanism.whatIsTheNudgePot: The contract's full ERC20 balance of nudgePaymentToken (an owner-configured token, e.g. USDC). Funded externally (e.g. a yield funnel routing USDC into this contract). The contract holds no per-call accounting of it; the pot IS whatever balanceOf(this) returns at call time.
nudgeMechanism.howPaidOut: Inside batchMint, AFTER the mint loop and AFTER the minter allowance is revoked, but BEFORE the dust refund sweep: if gate clears, transfers the ENTIRE nudgePaymentToken.balanceOf(this) to the caller-chosen `recipient` and emits NudgePaid. Full-drain semantics — first qualifying caller in any block takes the whole pot.
gateConditions: Up-front invariant: nudgePaymentToken must != derived paymentToken, else BatchMint__NudgeTokenMatchesPaymentToken reverts before any funds move.
callerControlledInputsIntoGate: count  -> directly controls whether count >= nudgeSize
recipient -> receives the entire nudge pot (caller can set to self)
paymentAmount -> must cover count real mints at dispatcher price or the batch reverts
ownerControlledInputsIntoGate: tokenMinter, dispatcherIndex (=> dispatcher => paymentToken => per-mint price)
nudgeMechanism.priorH01: value-blind nudge gate: attacker passed a caller-CHOSEN cheap/zero-price minter/dispatcher, faked `count` cheap mints to clear `count >= nudgeSize`, and drained the nudge pot without paying real mint cost.
nudgeMechanism.h01FixInThisDiff: Both the minter (already pinned in ab07199) and the dispatcher index (NEW in 031ffda) are now owner-pinned state; paymentToken is DERIVED from the pinned dispatcher's primeToken() rather than caller-supplied. The caller can no longer point batchMint at a cheap/zero dispatcher of their choosing. To clear `count >= nudgeSize` the attacker must now genuinely call the pinned, real minter.mint() `count` times, each pulling the pinned dispatcher's ramping price from msg.sender.
nudgeMechanism.residualConcern: The gate is STILL purely numeric (count >= nudgeSize) and remains VALUE-BLIND in the sense that it never compares the nudge payout to the amount the caller actually paid. The fix relies entirely on the owner pinning a dispatcher whose primeToken/price make `count >= nudgeSize` mints cost more than the pot. If the owner ever pins (or NFTMinterV2 ever holds) a dispatcher index whose config.price == 0, the inner mint pulls 0 tokens per iteration (NFTMinterV2._executeMint does NOT require price > 0 — see crossContractDependencies), and the attacker clears the gate for ~free and drains the pot again. This is now an OWNER-CONFIGURATION / cross-contract invariant rather than a caller-choice bug. Final adjudication is interaction-level.

diffSummary.storyContext: 031ffda = story-014 'Pin dispatcherIndex + derive paymentToken from dispatcher prime token'. Builds on ab07199 = story-013 which had already pinned the minter, added rescueERC20 + global pauser.
diffSummary.signatureChange: batchMint(IERC20 paymentToken, uint256 dispatcherIndex, uint256 count, address recipient, uint256 paymentAmount)  ->  batchMint(uint256 count, address recipient, uint256 paymentAmount). Removed BOTH the caller-supplied paymentToken AND the caller-supplied dispatcherIndex.
diffSummary.newState: Added `uint256 public dispatcherIndex` (owner-set, 0 = disabled sentinel) + setDispatcherIndex(onlyOwner) + DispatcherIndexSet event + BatchMint__DispatcherNotConfigured error.
diffSummary.logicChange: batchMint now: (1) reads owner-pinned dispatcherIndex, reverts DispatcherNotConfigured if 0; (2) resolves dispatcher = INFTMinterV2(minter).configs(dispatcherIndex).dispatcher, reverts if zero; (3) derives paymentToken = ITokenDispatcherV2(dispatcher).primeToken(). The nudge!=payment guard and all downstream logic are unchanged except they now operate on the derived token.
diffSummary.wasPriceValueValidationAdded: NO. No price>0 / value-vs-payout check was added. The gate remains `count >= nudgeSize` with no comparison of nudge payout to caller spend.
diffSummary.wasGateChanged: NO. The nudge gate itself (nudgeSize!=0 && count>=nudgeSize && token configured && balance!=0) is byte-for-byte unchanged. What changed is that the caller can no longer choose a cheap/zero dispatcher to make clearing that gate cheap.
diffSummary.netEffect: The diff removes the CALLER's ability to pick the value source (minter+dispatcher+token), converting H-01 from a permissionless caller-choice drain into a problem fully bounded by owner configuration + the trusted minter's registered dispatcher set. It does NOT add intrinsic value validation.

crossContractDependencies.criticalObservation: NFTMinterV2._executeMint (line 170-201) resolves token = dispatcher.primeToken() and does `IERC20(token).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, dispatcher, price)` where price = config.price. There is NO require(price > 0). The header comment claims an 'H-01 fix' but that fix is only about token SPOOFING (caller can't name the token), NOT about price being zero. A dispatcher registered/configured with price == 0 pulls 0 tokens per mint -> batchMint can clear count>=nudgeSize at zero real cost.
crossContractDependencies.implication: The phoenix-nft-staking H-01 'fix' depends on an UNVERIFIED sibling invariant: that the pinned dispatcherIndex always has config.price > 0 and config.disabled == false. registerDispatcher accepts initialPrice with no >0 check; setPrice can set 0. This is the residual cross-contract drain path and MUST be the focus of interaction analysis.

crossContractDependencies.criticalObservation: primeToken() is the sole authoritative source of paymentToken now. If a registered dispatcher returns a primeToken that equals nudgePaymentToken, batchMint reverts up-front (config invariant). If it returns address(0) or a non-contract, safeTransferFrom reverts (whole batch rolls back).
Global Pauser integration via custom onlyPauser + OZ Pausable hybrid, mirroring NFTStaker. Only batchMint is whenNotPaused-gated.

trustAssumptions: Owner pins tokenMinter to the genuine NFTMinterV2 and dispatcherIndex to a dispatcher whose config.price > 0 and disabled == false.
The pinned dispatcher's primeToken() is a standard ERC20 (no fee-on-transfer beyond what NFTMinterV2 already handles; no rebasing).
nudgePaymentToken differs from the pinned dispatcher's primeToken (deploy-time config invariant, enforced per-call as a revert).
Owner is trusted not to drain the nudge pot via rescueERC20 or via reconfiguring nudge setters (acknowledged centralization).
pauser address is the trusted global Pauser.
